extracted.intended_audience: readers, prospective contributors/writers, and partners/advertisers interested in Longreads
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and site policies from Longreads about the kinds of longform nonfiction work they publish and the rules for contributing or interacting with their content. Covers editorial focus, accepted formats, submission/contact pointers, and content/AI-sharing policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial focus: longform nonfiction storytelling
rubrics_metrics.description: Longreads, founded in 2009, is dedicated to finding and sharing the best longform nonfiction storytelling on the web.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site’s mission is to publish and surface high-quality longform nonfiction; editorial decisions are oriented toward that goal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted content types / formats
rubrics_metrics.description: We publish personal and reported essays, criticism, reading lists, and occasional book excerpts, interviews, and more in-depth features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the primary formats editors select for Longreads; examples and editors’ recent picks (with word counts) are provided on the page as indicators of the kinds of work they highlight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission policy — unsolicited drafts/pitches
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For writers interested in contributing, the page directs them to visit the Submissions page for guidelines and more on what editors look for — consult that page for the actionable submission process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on generative-AI–authored stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Longreads does not publish stories written using generative AI applications such as ChatGPT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a strict content standard for publication: work produced by generative-AI tools is not accepted. The site also takes steps (see robots.txt) to restrict AI crawlers from indexing/sharing their content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content-sharing and crawler policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Longreads opts out of sharing site content with third parties whenever possible and has added all known AI crawlers to the “disallow” list in our robots.txt file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a policy to limit redistribution and automated scraping/indexing of site content; it affects how content may be repurposed or accessed by third parties and tools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding / reader-supported model
rubrics_metrics.description: Our stories are funded with support from our readers. For every dollar you contribute to the Longreads Story Fund, our parent company Automattic matches it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Longreads is reader-supported and discloses its matching policy; membership/contribution options and the Story Fund are how editorial work is financed.
